title: Ty Simpson, 5 Buckeyes among 16 who will attend NFL Draft in Pittsburgh
content:
A total of 16 prospects, including five Ohio State Buckeyes and just one quarterback, will attend the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft in person the night of Thursday, April 23, in Pittsburgh.

The NFL announced the list of attendees Thursday, with Ohio State the leader among the three colleges sending multiple players to the event. Miami and Alabama are both sending two apiece, including Crimson Tide quarterback Ty Simpson, who will be the only QB in attendance.

Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza was notably not on the list of attendees. The Heisman Trophy winner is widely expected to be selected with the No. 1 pick by the Las Vegas Raiders and newly hired head coach Klint Kubiak. Simpson, however, is not considered a lock to be taken in the first round and was rated the No. 42 prospect in the draft by The Athletic’s Dane Brugler in “The Beast.”

USC receiver Makai Lemon joins the five Buckeyes to make six Big Ten players expected to attend, which is the most of any conference and narrowly leads the SEC, which will send five players.

The 16 players revealed by the NFL are:

David Bailey, LB, Texas Tech
Rueben Bain Jr., DE, Miami (Fla.)
Mansoor Delane, DB, LSU
Caleb Downs, DB, Ohio State
Keldric Faulk, DE, Auburn
Colton Hood, DB, Tennessee
Makai Lemon, WR, USC
Jeremiyah Love, RB, Notre Dame
Francis Mauigoa, OL, Miami (Fla.)
Kayden McDonald, DT, Ohio State
Kadyn Proctor, T, Alabama
Arvell Reese, LB, Ohio State
Ty Simpson, QB, Alabama
Sonny Styles, LB, Ohio State
Carnell Tate, WR, Ohio State
Jordyn Tyson, WR, Arizona State

The NFL invites prospects to attend the draft in person each year, where they can walk on stage after their selection and shake hands with commissioner Roger Goodell. However, the number of prospects who accept the invitation has declined in recent years due to numerous factors.

News of Mendoza’s plans not to attend the event emerged earlier this week, setting up the possibility of the No. 1 pick not being in attendance for the first time since Georgia edge rusher Travon Walker was selected with the top pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2022. Walker opted to watch the proceedings with friends and family in Atlanta instead of making the journey to Las Vegas.

Another notable absence this year will be Utah offensive lineman Spencer Fano, who Brugler ranked as the No. 8 prospect. Fano was a two-time All-American for Utah.

This year’s 16 attendees will be one fewer than last year’s in-person count in Green Bay, but the number is not the least in recent memory. In 2024, only 13 players attended the draft in Detroit, when Caleb Williams was taken at No. 1 by the Chicago Bears out of USC. The last quarterback taken No. 1 to not attend the draft was Clemson’s Trevor Lawrence in 2021, when he was picked by Jacksonville. Lawrence watched the event from South Carolina with family and friends.

An average of 24 players attended the green room during the draft’s first 10 years under the three-day format starting in 2010. Average attendance has dropped to 16 per year since no one attended the virtual 2020 NFL Draft during the COVID-19 pandemic. The lowest since the shift to a three-day draft was 12 in Cleveland in 2021.

The draft begins with the first round on Thursday, April 23, and continues with Rounds 2-3 on Friday, April 24. The draft concludes Saturday, April 25, with Rounds 4-7.
